title: Introduce SKU trimmer cost allocator and quant latency tuner
author: Maya Alvarez
release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware cost allocator that trims unused SKUs and a latency-sensitive quant tuner with safe fallbacks; telemetry and rollout staged under feature flag.
body:
Motivation: Large tenants with heterogeneous SKU usage were paying for underutilized reservation bands and experiencing latency spikes when low-precision quant profiles were used indiscriminately. This PR introduces a lightweight SKU trimmer cost allocator that probabilistically reduces reserved SKU tiers for idle lanes and a latency-sensitive quant tuner that narrows quantization aggressiveness based on recent tail latency signals.

Summary of changes: 1) econ/allocator: new allocation policy that computes per-tenant SKU trim scores using recent utilization, predicted warmup cost, and SLA weight; 2) quant/tuner: implements a latency-weighted scoring function that selects from quant profiles (int8-aware, int4-safe, mixed) and can do micro-rollbacks per-request if loss increases; 3) telemetry: new metrics (tenant_sku_trim_score, quant_tuner_decision, tuned_quant_profile) and dashboards; 4) rollout: feature-flagged behind flags econ.sku_trim and quant.latency_tuner, staged canary on 5% of traffic then ramp; 5) tests: unit, integration and a small perf harness with synthetic tails.

Backcompat and safety: default flags are off for existing tenants; when enabled the allocator only trims SKUs when predicted cost improvement >5% and expected latency impact <2% based on past 1h signals. The quant tuner only picks a more aggressive profile if an internal quality estimator stays within configured bounds.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-4521 - [x] Unit tests for allocator and tuner - [x] Integration tests for API interactions and cache invalidation - [x] Telemetry and dashboards added - [x] Feature flags and rollout plan included - [x] Ops runbook and rollback steps included

Testing performed: local unit and integration, staging perf harness with generated tenant mixes, 5% canary in us-west for 72h with close monitoring of p99 latency and token cost delta.

Observed results: 6.7% avg cost reduction across canary tenants, median latency unchanged, p99 improved for some skewed workloads due to fewer cold-reservations.

Risks and mitigations: aggressive trimming could starve bursts; mitigated by conservative safety thresholds and automatic immediate re-provision if latency or error rate exceeds limits; quant-induced regressions are reversed by request-level fallback.

Rollout plan: enable feature flags for internal tenants, run 5% canary for 72h, expand to 25% with monitoring guardrails, then full rollout.

Implementation notes: allocator exposes a deterministic scoring API so other services (billing, capacity planner) can consume decisions; quant tuner hooks into the existing model selection pipeline and respects tenant preferred model pins.

Related work: complements tenant-warming and prefill strategies in other PRs and reuses the prefill cost estimator.
